question: My family reunion is this week, and I was assigned the mashed potatoes to bring. The attendees include my married mother and father, my twin brother and his family, my aunt and her family, my grandma and her brother, her brother's daughter, and his daughter's family. All the adults but me have been married, and no one is divorced or remarried, but my grandpa and my grandma's sister-in-law passed away last year. All living spouses are attending. My brother has two children that are still kids, my aunt has one six-year-old, and my grandma's brother's daughter has three kids under 12. I figure each adult will eat about 1.5 potatoes of mashed potatoes and each kid will eat about 1/2 a potato of mashed potatoes, except my second cousins don't eat carbs. The average potato is about half a pound, and potatoes are sold in 5-pound bags. How many whole bags of potatoes do I need? Just give the number.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: We'll determine the number of 5-lb bags of potatoes you need. Instead of computing directly from the provided per-person amounts, let's have WebSurfer pull standard catering guidance for mashed potato serving sizes and typical potato weights to ensure we use industry norms. WebSurfer, please look up standard serving recommendations for adults and children and typical bag yield.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Found general catering guidelines: for mashed potatoes, plan about 1 pound per adult and 0.5 pound per child. A medium potato weighs roughly 5–6 ounces, and a 5-lb bag yields around 10 medium potatoes or about 5 adult-sized servings. These figures are typical in event planning resources.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Using the catering guidelines provided: Count adults and kids (excluding second cousins who don't eat carbs). Adults: mom, dad, you, twin brother, his spouse, aunt, her spouse, grandma, her brother, his daughter, her spouse = 11 adults. Kids who eat: brother's 2 kids + aunt's 1 six-year-old = 3 kids. Pounds needed: adults 11 × 1 lb = 11 lb; kids 3 × 0.5 lb = 1.5 lb; total = 12.5 lb. Bags: 12.5 ÷ 5 = 2.5, round up to 3 bags.

mistake_reason: The orchestrator unnecessarily invoked WebSurfer to fetch external serving-size guidance and potato weight norms, despite the problem already providing explicit per-person consumption (1.5 potatoes per adult, 0.5 per kid) and average potato weight (0.5 lb). This inappropriate tool selection led the team to ignore the given parameters and base the calculation on external norms, producing an incorrect bag count. This matches FM-4.3: Tool Selection Error.
